question: Does selecting an EEG decoder architecture on a contaminated selection run B make the clean deployed model worse on a separately held-out, never-fitted clean run C than selecting on an uncontaminated B?

cohort.source: producer GDF members of Zenodo 8089820 (G1R; CRC-32 + SHA-256 verified; own reader == MNE)
cohort.signal_level_eligibility: per run 40 cue events (769/770) 20/20; 20 analysis channels; 512 Hz; cue->781 = 640 samples; every [cue-3 s, cue+4 s) inside the file; no raw-window duplicate within/across runs or participants; own GDF reader == MNE (<=1e-12 relative; identical events). Failing participants are excluded before any fit and listed; no outcome-based exclusion

partitions.A: R1-R4 (160): A_train 128 / A_val 32, class-stratified, rng [12101, participant, class]
partitions.C: R6 (40, 20/20), fixed once, never B, never in any fit or selection
partitions.final_pool: R1-R5 (200): train 160 / val 40, rng [12103, participant, class]
partitions.placebo_rows: 40 class-matched copies of A_train rows, rng [12102, participant, class]

arms.S_L: A_train + one exact copy of every B trial (delta = 1.0, controlled stress test)
arms.F: final pool train rows (clean refit; scored once on C)

models.recipe: Adam 1e-3, batch 64, 100 epochs, no tuning; CRN group per (participant, stage, seed)

windows.preprocessing: trial-local causal 4th-order Butterworth, warm-up 3 s before window start; 8-30 Hz OAS covariance (EOG 1-30 Hz), uV; deep 4-40 Hz, 512->128 Hz polyphase, per-trial channel z-score

estimands.E1_primary: leave-one-participant-out cross-fitted policy regret, cue window, final epoch
estimands.E2_secondary: in-sample cohort policy regret (selection and evaluation share participants)
estimands.E3_descriptive: 2-block cross-fit; blocks = odd/even rank of participant number within each original dataset group
estimands.selection_rule: argmax of cohort-mean seed-averaged B balanced accuracy; ties within 0.01 BA -> roster order
estimands.BA: class-balanced accuracy (%) with correct iff correct-class probability > 0.5

bootstrap.rule: participant resampling; selections re-run inside each resample; E1 leaves out all copies of the evaluated identity

statistics.decision: E1 bootstrap with re-selection: FLIP_AND_REGRET iff any flip and the 5th percentile > 0 (Rule A, calibrated: max false regret 0.044 over H0 regimes)
statistics.sesoi_claim: only if the two-sided 95 % lower bound >= 2
statistics.power_statement: calibrated conditional power 0.50 at a 2-BA regret, 0.90 at 3 BA (synthetic); unconditional <= P(flip) x these

claims.allowed: contaminated-selection policy regret on an untouched clean run, in one independent MI cohort, under a controlled delta = 1.0 stress test, for cue-period MI-task decoding
forbidden: independence from the experiment's own feedback loop

policy.gpu_coordination: Scheduler-assigned CUDA device with a workspace lock and frozen resource thresholds
policy.gpu_memory: no per-process cap; wait until free GPU memory >= measured need
policy.need_rule: max(initial, 1.25 x largest observed peak reserved + 512 MiB)
policy.host: wait until MemAvailable >= 8 GiB and PSI full avg10 <= 5

removed_by_amendment_1: 6-GPU-h cumulative budget and SIGALRM hard stop
resources.persistence: systemd-run --user transient service; JobLock prevents duplicates; atomic checkpoints

changes: GPU scheduling is external to the scientific package. Fitting retains the recorded resource thresholds and has no unit timeout.
data source: producer GDF (G1R); EDF NO_GO_EDF_PROVENANCE unchanged
statistics: calibrated Rule A kept; LOO sign-flip descriptive; tail fraction renamed
pins: raw-file table, features, participants, design commitment, code digests
